st: Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef well on all sides for 8 minutes, then remove it to a plate.
Cook the onions and garlic in the same pot for 5 minutes until soft. Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes until it darkens.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until they break down into a thick sauce.
Return the beef to the pot with the bouillon cube, thyme, salt, pepper and the whole chili. Pour in [[6 cups]] water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 45 minutes until the beef is tender.
Add the carrots and cabbage and simmer for 15 minutes until soft. Lift the meat and vegetables out onto a plate and keep them warm.
Measure out [[5 cups]] of the broth, topping up with water if needed, and return it to the pot. Bring to a boil.
Stir in the rice, cover, lower the heat as far as it goes, and cook for 20 minutes until the rice is tender and has absorbed the red broth.
Rest the rice off the heat for 5 minutes, then fluff. Serve topped with the beef and vegetables.

ing: soaked and flaked, or smoked fish
st: Soak the dried fish in warm water for 10 minutes, then flake it and remove any bones.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4 minutes, then add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the okra, fish, chili and [[2 cups]] water. Simmer for 20 minutes, season with salt, and keep warm.
For the tô, bring [[3 cups]] water to a boil in a heavy pot. Mix [[0.5 cup]] of the millet flour with [[1 cup]] cold water until smooth.
Stir the flour mixture into the boiling water and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, to make a thin paste.
Mix the remaining [[1 cup]] millet flour with the corn flour. Add it gradually while beating hard with a wooden spoon so no lumps form.
Keep beating over low heat for 5 to 8 minutes until the mixture is very thick and pulls cleanly from the pot. Cover for 3 minutes.
With wet hands, shape the tô into smooth balls. Serve hot with the okra sauce.
Cut 2 or 3 shallow slashes in each piece of chicken so the marinade soaks in.
Mix the onion, garlic, ginger, mustard, lemon juice, chili, [[2 tbsp]] oil, pepper and salt in a bowl.
Rub the marinade all over the chicken, cover, and refrigerate for 2 hours.
Heat a grill to medium, or heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Wipe the extra marinade off the surface, and brush the chicken with the remaining [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Grill for 35 to 40 minutes, turning every 10 minutes, or roast on a rack for 40 minutes, until the skin is browned.
Check that the thickest part reaches 165°F (74°C) and the juices run clear. Rest for 5 minutes.
Serve with sliced onions, fries or rice.
Season the chicken with salt. Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken for 4 minutes per side. Remove it.
Cook the onion and garlic in the same pot for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and tomatoes and cook for 8 minutes until thick and oily.
Return the chicken to the pot with the whole chili and [[2 cups]] hot water. Cover and simmer for 25 minutes.
In a bowl, whisk the peanut butter with [[1 cup]] hot water and a ladle of the broth until smooth.
Stir the peanut mixture into the pot. Simmer uncovered on low for 20 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce thickens and oil rises to the top.
Check that the chicken has reached 165°F (74°C) and season with salt. Serve over rice or tô.

ing: soaked and flaked, or smoked fish
st: Soak the dried fish in warm water for 10 minutes, then flake it and remove any bones.
Put the beef in a pot with [[3 cups]] water and a little salt. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 40 minutes until tender.
Heat the oil in a second pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 6 minutes until they soften and thicken.
Pour in the beef with about half of its broth. Add the fish and whole chili.
Add the okra and simmer, uncovered, for 12 to 15 minutes until the sauce is thick and slippery.
Season with salt and serve hot with tô or rice.

ing: soaked and flaked, or smoked fish
st: Soak the dried fish in warm water for 10 minutes, then flake it and remove any bones.
Put the rice in a pot with [[3 cups]] water and a little salt. Bring to a boil, cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 18 minutes until tender.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the spinach in handfuls, stirring until it wilts, about 5 minutes.
Add the fish, soumbala, chili and [[1.5 cups]] water. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the ground peanuts and cook uncovered for 10 minutes more until thick and fragrant.
Taste and adjust the salt. Serve the stew over the rice.
Whisk the millet flour with [[1 cup]] cold water until smooth.
Bring [[3 cups]] water to a boil in a pot and stir in the flour mixture slowly.
Cook over medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring, until thickened and no longer raw-tasting. Let it cool for 20 minutes.
Stir in the ginger, tamarind paste, sugar, lemon juice and salt until dissolved.
Add [[2 cups]] cold water and whisk until it is a pourable drink.
Chill for at least 30 minutes.
Stir well before pouring, since the millet settles. Serve cold.
